classes.resume: The Command Center starts it again on its latest session.
classes.why: Every result ends there, so nothing may collect it.

classes.is: A monitor, shell or editor the Command Center opened beside a thread: in no tab, with no parent, named `<kind>-<thread address>`.
classes.closes: With its thread: the Command Center ends it once that thread is gone, and the worktree cleanup ends it with the thread of a merged or closed pull request.
classes.resume: Opening the thread's monitor, shell or editor starts a new one.
classes.why: It exists only to look at one thread.

classes.is: A terminal that reports no agent status, or one on another machine.
classes.closes: Never by this policy. One that is the child of an agent ends with that agent, as hc does for every child.
classes.practice: A collector reaps only what it can identify
classes.why: Without a status, an idle shell and a running build look the same.

classes.is: An agent another terminal started as its hc child (`hc run` from inside that terminal).
classes.closes: {helper} min after its owner received the result of its only turn; {reusedHelper} min once its owner has sent it back to work; at once when its owner is gone. Received means its owner read its screen after it finished (pi stamps each `hc read` in the {read} label) or started or ended a turn after it finished. Without a recorded read, a helper stays while its owner is working, blocked or in error, however long: an owner in the middle of a turn can still read its screen.
classes.trace: A line in the closed index. Its result sits in its owner's context, and `hc read <terminal>` still prints its last screen.
classes.resume: `agent-lifecycle reopen <terminal>` restarts its conversation under the same name and owner, for Claude Code and for a pi session that published its {session} label.
classes.practice: Time-to-live after completion, on a lease each use renews
classes.why: A helper has one job, and nobody but its owner reads the result.

classes.is: An agent in a tab of its own, with no parent. Its {owner} label names the terminal that opened the tab, when one did.
classes.closes: {thread} min after its last result was received, and only if its conversation can be resumed. Received means the terminal its {owner} label names read its screen or started or ended a turn after the thread finished, or the person looked at it. A thread of a repository also closes with its worktree when its pull request is merged or closed.
classes.trace: A trace file written before the close: last screen, folder, branch and the reopen command, listed in the closed index. A merged or closed pull request is the trace of its thread.
classes.resume: `agent-lifecycle reopen <terminal>` opens a tab in the same folder and space on the same conversation.
classes.practice: Scale to zero: the session file is the durable state, the terminal a process that can restart cold
classes.why: The person may come back to a task, and never needs its idle process.

classes.is: A linked worktree a helper or an owned thread worked in, other than its owner's own.
classes.closes: Removed with its branch once no terminal is open in it, nothing in it is uncommitted or untracked, and another local branch holds its commits. Tried again every {worktreeRetry} min until then. One whose branch has a pull request is left to that pull request.
classes.trace: A line in the closed index when removed; listed there with the reason while it stays.
classes.resume: `git worktree add` from the branch that holds its commits.
classes.why: Work reachable from another branch is safe to drop, and only that work.

rules: A terminal stays open while it is working, blocked or in error.

It stays open while its {waiting} label names work that will wake it: pi publishes it from its subagents, wait subscriptions and awaited shell jobs, Claude Code from its background tasks and scheduled wakeups (`~/.claude/hooks/herdr-waiting.sh`, on every turn end).

It stays open while its {unfinished} label reports open items of its task: pi publishes it from the session's goal checklist, so an agent that ended its turn on a question stays until the answer lets it finish. An orphan helper is the exception: nobody is left to answer it.
It stays open while the person is on it: the focused agent, the tab on screen, or a terminal the Command Center shows.
It stays open while a terminal it started still works, and while a child that would end with it is unreported, kept, watched or finished less than its own lease ago.
It stays open while its {keep} label is set: `agent-lifecycle keep <terminal>`.
A lease starts when the sweeper first sees the result received, and restarts with every new turn and every look by the person.
A terminal closes on the second sweep that finds it eligible, at least {confirm} s after the first, with its screen unchanged in between.
Closing ends the program and keeps the record: `hc read <terminal>` prints its last screen until someone removes it.
